skill.name: nmap
skill.description: Plan and analyze authorized Nmap reconnaissance, including port discovery, service detection, NSE checks, output capture, and IoT-focused follow-up scans.
skill.summary: Guide authorized Nmap scans and structured service analysis.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: The skill contains actionable Nmap commands for privileged, broad, stealth, vulnerability, protocol, and brute-force scans. Markdown, hard-link, and private-address alerts are false positives, but confirmed scan guidance creates substantial dual-use risk. Authorization is advisory, while evasion techniques and automatic privileged scanning remain operational instructions.

remediation.issue: Authorization and scope are not enforced before scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit written-authorization confirmation, exact targets, exclusions, timing, and stop conditions before generating or executing any scan.

remediation.issue: The skill provides detection-evasion and brute-force guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove stealth, IDS-evasion, fragmentation, trusted-source-port, brute-force, and URL-brute instructions. Limit NSE guidance to approved low-impact scripts.

remediation.issue: The default workflow uses sudo and scans every port.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a narrow unprivileged scan with rate limits. Require separate approval for sudo, all-port, UDP, operating-system, and vulnerability scans.

static_findings.snippet: **IMPORTANT**: Always save nmap output to an organized directory structure. By default, use `./nmap-
- `-Pn`: Skip host discovery, treat host as online
- `-p <OPEN_PORT_LIST>`: Only scan the ports found to be open (e.g., `-p 23,80,443,554,8000`)
- `-sC`: Run default NSE scripts for additional enumeration
Or parse from .nmap file (matches the STATE column exactly, so `open|filtered` ports are excluded):
- `-oA`: Output in all formats (normal, XML, grepable)
- `-sS`: SYN stealth scan (doesn't complete TCP handshake)
- `--top-ports 100`: Scan top 100 UDP ports (UDP scanning is slow)
- `-A`: Enable OS detection, version detection, script scanning, traceroute
- `-T4`: Aggressive timing template (faster but more detectable)
- `--script vuln`: Run NSE vulnerability detection scripts
Always use `-oA <prefix>` to generate all three formats:
- `.xml` - XML format for parsing/importing into tools
**Fast scans**: Use `-T4` when speed is important and network can handle it
Always save to an organized output directory (default `./nmap-output/`). See the Implementation Work
- Consider using `--source-port 53` or other trusted ports

content.value_statement: Unknown services and exposed ports make authorized network assessment difficult. This skill guides structured Nmap scans, output capture, service detection, and result review.
actual_capabilities: Builds two-phase Nmap workflows for full-port discovery and targeted service detection.
Provides quick, comprehensive, SYN, UDP, aggressive, vulnerability, and operating system scan options.
Shows how to save normal, XML, and grepable output with the Nmap -oA option.
Parses saved results to identify open ports, service versions, and vulnerability indicators.
Suggests targeted NSE checks for web, SSH, RTSP, ONVIF, UPnP, MQTT, and Modbus services.
limitations: Requires Nmap and appropriate local privileges; several scan types require root access.
Does not verify ownership, authorization, target scope, or legal permission.
Scan accuracy depends on filtering, rate limits, network conditions, and target behavior.
Aggressive, UDP, vulnerability, and brute-force scans may disrupt services or trigger monitoring.

use_cases.title: Inventory Authorized Assets
use_cases.description: Discover exposed ports and identify services on approved internal hosts while preserving scan evidence.

use_cases.title: Assess IoT Services
use_cases.description: Map web, RTSP, MQTT, UPnP, and Modbus services during an authorized device assessment.

use_cases.title: Investigate Network Exposure
use_cases.description: Compare expected services with observed ports and document unexpected exposure for remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Low-Impact Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a low-impact Nmap scan for authorized host [target]. Confirm scope, explain selected options, and save all output under [directory].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Two-Phase Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a two-phase Nmap workflow for authorized target [target]. Discover ports, inspect detected services, and summarize expected output files.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Saved Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the saved Nmap results from [file]. List open ports, identified versions, uncertain fingerprints, and recommended low-impact follow-up checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design an IoT Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authorized IoT assessment for [target] within [scope]. Include rate limits, targeted NSE categories, stop conditions, evidence capture, and risk controls.

output_examples.input: Assess authorized host 10.0.0.25 with low impact.
output: Scope check: one approved private host with no excluded ports supplied.
Plan: begin with limited discovery, save all formats, then inspect only confirmed open ports.
Safety: use conservative timing and stop if the host becomes unstable.

output_examples.input: Summarize a saved scan showing ports 22, 80, and 443.
output_examples.output: The host exposes remote administration and two web services. Validate versions, transport security, ownership, and whether each service is expected.

output_examples.input: Plan follow-up checks for an authorized camera with HTTP and RTSP.
output_examples.output: Review HTTP methods and RTSP capabilities with approved low-impact scripts. Record evidence and avoid brute-force checks unless separately authorized.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, exact targets, exclusions, timing, and stop conditions before every scan.
Start with the least intrusive scan that answers the question, then expand only with explicit approval.
Save outputs securely, record parameters and timestamps, and validate automated findings before reporting.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public or third-party systems without documented permission.
Do not default to stealth, fragmentation, brute-force, or vulnerability scripts on production systems.
Do not run broad privileged scans when a narrow unprivileged check is sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Nmap?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and commands that an agent may execute when Nmap, tools, and permissions are available.

faq.question: Do I need authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. Obtain documented permission and confirm the exact target scope before scanning any host or network.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance uses Nmap output options for normal, XML, and grepable files.

faq.question: When is root access required?
faq.answer: SYN, UDP, operating-system detection, and other raw-packet features commonly require elevated privileges.

faq.question: Can it assess IoT devices?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes targeted guidance for RTSP, ONVIF-related web services, UPnP, MQTT, and Modbus.

faq.question: Are scan findings definitive?
faq.answer: No. Firewalls, rate limits, service behavior, and fingerprint uncertainty can produce incomplete or inaccurate results.
